newsitem.title: INDIA: India Shaw sells 1 mln cases of beer.
newsitem.headline: India Shaw sells 1 mln cases of beer.

text.p: India's Shaw Wallace and Co said on Monday it had sold more than one million cases of beer in March, and forecast that sales would stay at the same monthly level for financial year 1997/98 (April-March).

"For the twelve-month period ended March 31, 1997, Shaw Wallace's beer sales volumes grew nearly 16 percent at a time when India's beer industry experienced a substantial degrowth of 5.5 percent," the firm said in a statement.

"The brewery division achieved a landmark last month when it crossed the one-million-case sales mark," the statement added. "Shaw Wallace is optimistic that ... the company will have an average beer sales at one-milion-cases per month for the whole year ahead."
Shaw Wallace said it had achieved its impressive sales volume inspite of severe financial and regulatory constraints.

"The market share of the company's brands grew 100 percent from 8.2 percent in 1993-94 to 16.5 percent in 1996-97," the statement added. "The operating profits of the company in the beer business rose nearly 51 percent."
Much of this growth has resulted from the firm's aggressive development of its beer business, which saw it buy five breweries and contract eight others during the early 90s.
Until 1993-94, Shaw Wallace's share in India's beer market had been around eight percent, with just two breweries, in western Maharashtra and Pondicherry to the south, the firm said.

"Shaw Wallace breweries division has recorded a compounded growth rate of 29 percent over the last three years. The corresponding figure for beer against the industry is a mere four percent," the statement said.
